MEASURED ON BEDROCK: caching WORKS, so this bug is specific to the direct-Anthropic path.

Raw boto3 converse with a 29,400-char repeated prefix + cachePoint, us-east-1:
  us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6  call-1 cacheWrite=6604   call-2/3 cacheRead=6604
  us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8    call-1 cacheWrite=11404  call-2/3 cacheRead=11404
End-to-end through rebar's bedrock_model.py path (19-call gate run):
  cache_read_tokens=542,723  cache_write_tokens=6,239

pydantic-ai's Bedrock adapter does map cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens (models/bedrock.py:676-682),
so these are real numbers, not defaults.

This reframes the bug: the cache_read=0/cache_write=0 rebar logs on claude-opus-4-8 is NOT a
model-capability fact, it is a direct-Anthropic-path fact. Moving that traffic to Bedrock fixes it.

Caveat: 2 of 19 calls (plan-review-coach, ticket-digest) still logged 'caching requested but had NO
effect'. Both were small one-off calls with no prior identical prefix, so that is expected behaviour
rather than the defect — worth encoding in the warning's floor so it stops crying wolf on them.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIXED (rebar-debug protocol, worktree `fix/7a79-cache-floor`) — the floor gate is in, with the
genuine detection preserved and the constant single-sourced.

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed, not read off source)

`warn_if_cache_ineffective`'s predicate had an UPPER-open lower bound only: `input_tokens > 0`.
A live probe drove the function with the exact per-call `input_tokens` values recorded in this
ticket (1822, 2184, 2317, 3140) plus 8192, all with zero/zero counters and
`caching_requested=True`. Every one emitted the identical warning — the 8192 (cacheable) case
and the four sub-floor (never-cacheable) cases were INDISTINGUISHABLE in the log. That is the
mechanism: the predicate cannot separate "a cacheable prompt silently failed to cache" (real,
actionable) from "the prompt was never cacheable" (expected, unactionable).

Legitimacy = `defect`, cited against the codebase's OWN design invariant: `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`
(pass1.py) already documents that a sub-floor prefix "never caches" and already suppresses cache
WARM-UP below it. The warning path simply never consulted the fact the warm-up path relies on.

## The fix

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — NEW shared home for `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096`, sited
  next to `cache_settings_for`: the module that already owns prompt-cache knowledge, and the
  lowest layer BOTH consumers already sit above. (The plan's first-named candidate; `config.py`
  would have made a per-model cache fact look like an operator knob.)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the literal becomes
  `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. The name and both historical
  call sites (:222, :496) are untouched. No cycle: `capabilities` imports only stdlib at module
  top. ONE definition, per the AC — no second literal, no hand-sync (unlike `DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`).
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — `input_tokens > 0` becomes
  `input_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. Signature UNCHANGED, so `runner.py:509` needed no
  edit (that file is owned by a parallel session).

Deliberately NOT done: the ticket's secondary suggestion to aggregate per-RUN instead of per-CALL.
The floor alone reduces the ~20 lines/run to zero when caching works, and a per-run aggregate is a
larger design change touching `usage_log`/`runner` (both owned by parallel sessions). Worth a
follow-up ticket only if per-call lines still prove noisy above the floor.

## RED confirmed first, and the test has teeth

NEW `tests/unit/test_cache_floor_warning.py` (11 cases). Pre-fix: 6 failed / 5 passed —
the 5 sub-floor cases failed on the intended assertion with the captured warning in the pytest
log (right reason, not an import/fixture error), and the single-source case failed with
`AttributeError: module 'rebar.llm.capabilities' has no attribute 'CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS'`
(also the right reason). Critically, the 4 above-floor cases and the "other silence reasons" case
were GREEN pre-fix and stayed green — that is the standing proof the genuine detection was never
weakened, only bounded.

Post-fix 11/11 green. Mutation check: re-seeding the exact root cause (`>= FLOOR` back to `> 0`)
returned the suite to 5 failed, then restored. The test is not a tautology.

The floor is imported FROM `pass1` in the test rather than restated as `4096`, so if the two
definitions ever drift apart again the boundary cases fail on their own.

## One pre-existing test had a real behavioral dependency — flagged, not silently bent

`tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py::test_warns_when_caching_was_requested_but_both_counters_are_zero`
pinned `input_tokens=4029` — which is itself BELOW the 4096 floor, so it went red on the fix. Raised
that one literal to 40290 (a realistic gate-prompt size); every assertion is intact
(`len(warnings) == 1`, model-name-in-message) and the docstring now says why a cacheable size is
required. A literal-for-literal expectation change, not a weakened test.

HONEST CONSEQUENCE, worth recording: the originally MEASURED opus-4-5 defect was observed at 4029
input tokens, i.e. sub-floor. Under the new contract that specific reading is classified as
expected rather than a defect. This is the correct call — 4029 tokens genuinely cannot cache, so
zero/zero there was never evidence of anything — but it does mean the narrowest form of the
original observation no longer trips the warning. The defect CLASS (a cacheable prompt that does
not cache) remains fully caught, which is the signal that has operator-actionable value.

## Gates

`make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0 (407 files). 576 passed across
`test_bedrock_provider` / `test_structured_run_seam` / `tests/unit/workflow/` /
`test_prompt_cache_split` / the new file; full `tests/unit` sweep run separately. Module-size cap
respected — largest touched file is `pass1.py` at 735 of 800.

Sibling sweep (root cause as a CLASS: a cache predicate reading zero counters as a defect without
a cacheability bound): every other `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` site in `src/` only
aggregates or reports the counters (`usage_log`, `sizing`, `voter`, `finalize`,
`runner.py:557` INFO line) — none interprets zero as a defect. No siblings.

## Replication

Driving the function exactly as `runner.py:509` does, with all five live-observed sub-floor
readings: zero warnings emitted. The above-floor zero/zero case: one warning, naming the model.
The original report no longer reproduces.

## Remaining AC (needs an operator, cannot be self-attested)

`[operator-attested]` a full `rebar review-plan` run emitting zero cache warnings while its
aggregate `cache_write_tokens > 0`. Unit-level evidence is complete; the live run needs real
provider credentials and a human attestation.

Not pushed — the orchestrator cherry-picks this onto the Gerrit stack.

ATTESTATION RECIPE — why the criterion is still open and exactly how to close it.

The AC wants a full rebar review-plan run emitting ZERO cache warnings when caching is working,
evidenced by the run's aggregate cache_write_tokens > 0.

A live plan-review WAS run this session (on 0d76, after the fix landed on origin/main) and its coverage
metrics recorded cache_write_tokens 39473 and cache_read_tokens 225616 — both well above zero, so
caching was demonstrably working. That is most of the evidence. It is NOT cited as satisfying the
criterion because the run was not captured in a form that also proves the ZERO-WARNINGS half: the
warning is emitted to the log stream, and that run's output was not retained for warning inspection.

RECIPE (a single run satisfies this AND 77ed's Pass-1 attestation):
  export REBAR_USAGE_LOG=/tmp/rebar_usage.jsonl
  rebar review-plan <any unblocked ticket> 2>&1 | tee /tmp/review_run.log
then cite, on this ticket: the aggregate cache_write_tokens from the verdict's coverage.metrics, the
absence of any warn_if_cache_ineffective line in /tmp/review_run.log, and a timestamp. Note the usage
log is OPT-IN — usage_log.py:29 ENV_VAR = 'REBAR_USAGE_LOG' — so without the export there is no
per-step attribution to cite.

Reminder from the fix itself: the 4096-token floor is model-dependent and documented as the OPUS
floor, so a run below it legitimately emits no warning and would not prove the criterion either way —
the cited run must be above the floor, as the 0d76 run's 39473 cache_write_tokens comfortably was.

compiled_state.description:
# The cache-ineffective warning cannot tell 'model does not cache' from 'prompt below the cacheable floor'

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:warn_if_cache_ineffective` (story 2932) warns when prompt caching was requested but both counters are zero:

```python
if (caching_requested
        and usage.get('cache_read_tokens', 0) == 0
        and usage.get('cache_write_tokens', 0) == 0
        and usage.get('input_tokens', 0) > 0):
```

It was added for a REAL defect: `opus-4-5` reports both counters zero while billing the full input, with no provider error. That defect is worth catching.

But the predicate has no lower bound, and the codebase ALREADY KNOWS there is one: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:45` defines `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` — 'the minimum prompt-prefix the anthropic cache will write/read (Opus 4.8 floor). Below this the parent-plan system prefix never caches.'

**Below 4096 tokens, zero/zero is the CORRECT and EXPECTED result, not a symptom.** The warning fires anyway and asserts the operator 'is paying full input price on every call' — which is true but not actionable, because no configuration change could make a sub-floor prompt cache.

## Observed (this session, both providers)

Every warning observed fired well under the floor:

| run | model | input_tokens | warned |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan-review 281f (direct Anthropic) | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | 2184 | yes |
| plan-review 281f (direct Anthropic) | `claude-opus-4-8` | 1822 – 3140 (≈20 calls) | yes, each |
| plan-review 281f (Bedrock) | `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | 2184, 2317 | yes |

**The decisive observation:** in the Bedrock run the aggregate usage for the same review was `cache_write_tokens: 2132`, `cache_read_tokens: 0` — i.e. caching DID engage in that run, on the call whose prefix cleared the floor — while the per-call warnings for the smaller calls simultaneously claimed caching 'had NO effect'. The warning therefore contradicts the run's own aggregate telemetry.

A single `rebar review-plan` emits roughly twenty of these lines.

## Why it matters

1. **Alarm fatigue on the one signal that catches silent cost bleed.** The warning's whole justification is that an ineffective cache is invisible without it. Firing ~20 times per gate run, almost always benignly, trains operators to filter it out — so when a model genuinely stops caching (the opus-4-5 case), the signal is already noise.
2. **It gets louder exactly at the cutover.** Post-Bedrock every gate run emits these, and they name the Bedrock model, so they will read as 'Bedrock broke caching' during precisely the window when the team is watching for Bedrock regressions. That is a false lead planted at the worst moment.
3. It contradicts the run's own aggregate usage numbers, which undermines trust in the telemetry generally.

## Approach (candidate, not a decision)

Gate the warning on the floor: only warn when `input_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, so it fires only where caching COULD have worked and demonstrably did not. The constant currently lives in `plan_review/pass1.py` while the warning lives in `llm/structured_run.py`, so it needs a shared home (`capabilities.py` or `config.py`) rather than a second literal — the epic already has one hand-synced duplicated constant (`DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`) and should not add another.

Consider also aggregating per RUN rather than per CALL: 'this run made N cacheable-size calls and none cached' is the actionable statement; a per-call line is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts NO warning is emitted when `caching_requested` and both counters are zero but `input_tokens` is below the floor
- [ ] a test asserts the warning IS still emitted above the floor with both counters zero (the opus-4-5 defect it exists for stays caught)
- [ ] the floor constant has ONE definition shared by `pass1.py` and `structured_run.py`, not a second literal
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full `rebar review-plan` run emits zero cache warnings when caching is working, evidenced by the run's aggregate `cache_write_tokens > 0`
